sanskrit: mṛtyur eko yama ekaḥ śarva ekaḥ śarur bhavaḥ | te naḥ kṛṇvantu bheṣajaṃ devasenābhyas pari ||
english: Death is one, Yama is one, Śarva is one, the arrow-hurler is Bhava — may they fashion healing for us, away from the divine hosts.

sanskrit: punar no yamaḥ pitṛbhir dadātu punar mitrāvaruṇā vāto agniḥ | aghamāro aghaśaṃsaḥ punar dāt punar no devī nirṛtir dadātu ||
english: May Yama restore us together with the Fathers; may Mitra and Varuṇa, Vāyu and Agni restore us; may the slayer of evil, the proclaimer of evil, restore us; may the goddess Nirṛti restore us once more.

sanskrit: yā devaiḥ prahiteṣuḥ patāt tapase vā mahase vāvasṛṣṭā | somas tvām asmad yāvayatu vidvān pitaro vā devahutā nṛcakṣasaḥ ||
english: The arrow that has flown dispatched by the gods, or that which has been released toward heat or toward the great power — may Soma the knowing drive it away from us, or the Fathers invoked by the gods, who behold mankind.

sanskrit: sahasrākṣo amartyaḥ pururūpa ihāvatu | sakhye ta ugra mā riṣaṃ sahaguḥ sahapūruṣaḥ ||
english: May the thousand-eyed immortal one, of manifold forms, protect here. In your friendship, O fierce one, may I come to no harm — you who are companion to the cow and companion to man.

sanskrit: yas te manyuḥ sahasrākṣa viṣeṇa pariṣicyate | tena tvam asmabhyaṃ mṛḍa śivo naḥ śambhur ā cara ||
english: The fury of yours, O Thousand-eyed one, that is poured round with poison — with that same fury be gracious to us; come to us as benign, as Śambhu.

sanskrit: mā te mayau sahasrākṣa bhāme bhūn māmakaṃ jagat | yo no dveṣṭi taṃ gaccha yaṃ dviṣmas taṃ jahi ||
english: May no world of mine fall under your wrath, O Thousand-eyed one, in your blazing fury. Go to him who hates us; strike down him whom we hate.

sanskrit: ye sthāsyāṃ prācyāṃ diśi hetayo nāma devās teṣāṃ vo agnir iṣavaḥ | te no mṛḍata te no 'dhi brūta tebhyo namas tebhyaḥ svāhā ||
english: Those gods who stand in the eastern quarter, named Hetayas — their arrows are Agni. May they show us mercy, may they speak on our behalf. Homage to them; svāhā to them.

sanskrit: ye sthāsyāṃ dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśy aviṣyavo nāma devās teṣaṃ va āpa iṣavaḥ | te no mṛḍata te no 'dhi brūta tebhyo namas tebhyaḥ svāhā ||
english: Those gods who stand in the southern quarter, named Aviṣyavaḥ — their arrows are the Waters. May they show us mercy, may they speak on our behalf. Homage to them; svāhā to them.

sanskrit: ye sthāsyāṃ pratīcyāṃ diśi virājo nāma devās teṣaṃ vaḥ kāma iṣavaḥ | te no mṛḍata te no 'dhi brūta tebhyo namas tebhyaḥ svāhā ||
english: Those gods who stand in the western quarter, named Virājaḥ — their arrows are Kāma. May they show us mercy, may they speak on our behalf. Homage to them; svāhā to them.

sanskrit: ye sthāsyām udīcyāṃ diśi pravidhyanto nāma devās teṣaṃ vo vāta iṣavaḥ | te no mṛḍata te no 'dhi brūta tebhyo namas tebhyaḥ svāhā ||
english: Those gods who stand in the northern quarter, named Pravidhyantaḥ — their arrows are Vāyu. May they show us mercy, may they speak on our behalf. Homage to them; svāhā to them.

sanskrit: ye sthāsyāṃ dhruvāyāṃ diśi vilimpā nāma devās teṣaṃ vo 'nnam iṣavaḥ | te no mṛḍata te no 'dhi brūta tebhyo namas tebhyaḥ svāhā ||
english: Those gods who stand in the fixed (nadir) quarter, named Vilimpāḥ — their arrows are Food. May they show us mercy, may they speak on our behalf. Homage to them; svāhā to them.

sanskrit: ye sthāsyām ūrdhvāyāṃ diśy aviṣyanto nāma devās teṣaṃ vo varṣam iṣavaḥ | te no mṛḍata te no 'dhi brūta tebhyo namas tebhyaḥ svāhā ||
english: Those gods who stand in the upper quarter, named Aviṣyantaḥ — their arrows are Rain. May they show us mercy, may they speak on our behalf. Homage to them; svāhā to them.

sanskrit: yo apsv antar yo vṛtre antar yaḥ puruṣe yo aśmani | ya āviveśauṣadhīr yo vanaspatīṃs tebhyo agnibhyo hutam astv etat ||
english: He who dwells within the Waters, he who dwells within Vṛtra, he who is in man, he who is in the stone — he who has entered into the herbs and into the trees of the forest: may this oblation be offered to those fires.

sanskrit: yaḥ some antar ya u goṣv antar ya āviṣṭo vayasi yo mṛgeṣu | ya āviveśa dvipado yaś catuṣpadas tebhyo agnibhyo hutam astv etat ||
english: He who dwells within Soma, he who dwells within cattle, he who has entered into birds and into wild beasts — he who has entered into two-footed creatures and into four-footed ones: may this oblation be offered to those fires.

sanskrit: ya indreṇa sarathaṃ saṃbabhūva vaiśvānara uta viśvadāvyaḥ | yaṃ johavīmi pṛtanāsuṣāsahiṃ tebhyo agnibhyo hutam astv etat ||
english: He who shares a chariot with Indra, Vaiśvānara the all-consuming one — him I invoke with repeated calls, the one who ever conquers in battles: may this oblation be offered to those fires.

sanskrit: yo devo viśvād yam u kāmam āhur yaṃ dātāraṃ pratigṛhṇantam āhuḥ | yo dhīraḥ śakraḥ paribhūr adābhyas tebhyo agnibhyo hutam astv etat ||
english: That god whom they call the all-devourer, whom they call Kāma, whom they call the giver and the receiver — he the wise, the mighty, the encompassing, the undeceivable: may this oblation be offered to those fires.

sanskrit: yaṃ tvā hotāraṃ manasābhisaṃvidus trayodaśa bhauvanāḥ pañca mānavāḥ | varcodhase yaśase sūnṛtāvate tebhyo agnibhyo hutam astv etat ||
english: Thee whom thirteen world-beings and five human ones recognized in mind as the hotar-priest — for the bearing of vital luster, for glory, for the one rich in true speech: may this oblation be offered to those fires.

sanskrit: ukṣānnāya vaśānnāya somapṛṣṭhāya vedhase | vaiśvānarasya jyeṣṭhebhyas tebhyo agnibhyo hutam astv etat ||
english: To him whose food is the bull, whose food is the cow, who bears Soma upon his back, the wise ordainer — to the eldest forms of Vaiśvānara: may this oblation be offered to those fires.

sanskrit: divaṃ pṛthivīm antarikṣaṃ ye vidyutam anusaṃcaranti | ye dikṣv antar ya u vāte antas tebhyo agnibhyo hutam astv etat ||
english: Those who move in succession through heaven, earth, and atmosphere, those who pursue the lightning — those who dwell within the quarters and those who dwell within the wind: may this oblation be offered to those fires.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatiṃ varuṇaṃ mitram agniṃ hiraṇyapāṇiṃ savitāram indram | viśvān devān aṅgiraso havāmaha imaṃ kravyādaṃ śamayantv agnim ||
english: Bṛhaspati, Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, the golden-handed Savitṛ, Indra — all the gods and the Aṅgirasas we invoke: may they appease this flesh-devouring fire.

sanskrit: śānto agniḥ kravyād atho puruṣareṣaṇaḥ | atho yo viśvadāvyas taṃ kravyādam aśīśamam ||
english: Appeased is the flesh-devouring fire, and also the man-seeking one. And that which is the all-devourer — that flesh-eating fire I have wholly pacified.
